raw_text:
Below is a 12‑week, pregnancy‑safe strength program designed for an advanced lifter at 20 weeks pregnant, cleared for moderate strength training. It honors standard pregnancy contraindications: no supine work after week 16, no 1RM/maximal attempts, no contact sports, and an emphasis on moderate intensity, breathing/bracing modifications, and symptom‑guided progression. The goal is to maintain strength, movement quality, and comfort through the second into early third trimester.

Global guidelines and guardrails
- Intensity/RPE: Work mostly at RPE 6–7 (about 65–75% of pre‑pregnancy 1RM). Leave 3–4 reps in reserve. No grinders or valsalva. Prioritize nasal or pursed‑lip exhale through effort.
- Volume: 3 sessions/week, 60–75 minutes. Total weekly hard sets per muscle group ~6–10, adjusted by symptoms.
- Temperature/hydration: Avoid overheating, ensure cool environment, drink before/during/after.
- Supine modifications: No flat‑on‑back after week 16. Swap benching to 30–45° incline or high‑incline machine; avoid prolonged supine. If any dizziness/tingling, stop and reposition.
- Core/pelvic floor: Emphasize diaphragmatic breathing, pelvic floor “bulge/relax” on inhale and “lift/gentle engage” on exhale. Avoid high‑pressure moves (heavy bilateral bracing, sit‑ups, crunches, loaded rotational crunches). Favor anti‑extension/anti‑rotation and side‑lying.
- Symptom stop rules: Stop any movement that triggers pelvic/low back pain, pubic symphysis pain, doming/coning along the midline, vaginal pressure, bleeding, fluid leakage, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, or contractions.
- Range of motion: Use pain‑free ROM; reduce depth or stance if pubic symphysis or SI discomfort occurs.
- Conditioning: Low‑impact options only (walking, incline treadmill, bike, elliptical). Keep conversational intensity.
- Recovery: 7–9 hours sleep, daily mobility 5–10 minutes, and light walking on non‑lift days.

Progression overview
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Re‑establish movement patterns, breathe/bracing, moderate loads, accommodate bump/ligament changes.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Maintain strength with slight load or volume progressions; prioritize unilateral stability and mid‑range strength.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Hold or slightly taper loads if needed; increase accessories for joint health and posture; emphasize birth‑supportive breathing and pelvic floor coordination.

Warm‑up template each session (10–12 minutes)
- Breath/reset: 2–3 minutes 90/90 or seated diaphragmatic breathing with pelvic floor coordination.
- Mobility: Thoracic openers, cat‑cow, half‑kneeling hip flexor with posterior pelvic tilt, adductor rock backs, ankle rocks.
- Activation: Banded lateral walks, bodyweight squats with exhale on rise, wall slides or band pull‑aparts.
- RPE ramp: 2–3 specific warm‑up sets to the day’s first main lift.

Session split
- Day A: Squat pattern + hinge accessory + vertical push/pull + core
- Day B: Hinge pattern + horizontal push/pull (incline) + single‑leg + core
- Day C: Unilateral squat/hinge focus + upper accessories + conditioning finisher

Exercise menu and substitutions (pregnancy‑friendly)
- Squat patterns: Safety bar squat, high‑bar box squat, front squat to box (light–moderate), goblet squat, landmine squat.
- Hinge patterns: Trap bar deadlift, RDL (bar or DB), landmine RDL, cable pull‑through, hip thrust (elevate torso vs. flat supine; or bench‑supported with short sets and monitoring).
- Unilateral: Split squats (rear‑foot elevated if comfortable), step‑ups, walking lunges (short stride), lateral step‑downs, single‑leg RDL (DB).
- Horizontal push: Incline DB or barbell press (30–45°), machine chest press (semi‑reclined), push‑ups to bar/box (elevated).
- Vertical push: Half‑kneeling or seated DB press (not fully supine), landmine press.
- Pulls: Chest‑supported row, 1‑arm DB row, cable row, lat pulldown, assisted pull‑ups.
- Core: Side planks (elevated if needed), Pallof press/holds, half‑kneeling anti‑rotation press, bird dog, modified dead bug (head/torso elevated), farmer carries, suitcase carries.
- Conditioning: 10–20 min easy‑moderate walk/bike/elliptical.

Intensity notation
- Use RPE 6–7 targets. If using percentages, 60–75% 1RM equivalent, but honor RPE and symptoms over numbers.
- Progression: If last week’s top sets felt ≤RPE6 and symptom‑free, add 2–2.5% load or 1–2 reps per set next time. Otherwise hold or reduce.

Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 (repattern, stabilize, build tolerance)
Week 1
- Day A
  - Safety bar squat: 4x5 @ RPE 6
  - DB RDL: 3x8 @ RPE 6–7
  - 1‑arm landmine press: 3x8/side @ RPE 6
  - Lat pulldown (medium grip): 3x8 @ RPE 6
  - Side plank (knees or feet): 3x20–30s/side
- Day B
  - Trap bar deadlift (low–mid handles): 4x4 @ RPE 6
  - Incline DB press (30–45°): 4x6 @ RPE 6
  - Chest‑supported row: 3x10 @ RPE 6
  - Split squat (flat rear foot): 3x8/side @ RPE 6
  - Pallof press: 3x10/side, 2–3s holds
- Day C
  - Front squat to box (just above parallel): 3x5 @ RPE 6
  - Cable pull‑through: 3x10 @ RPE 6
  - Seated DB overhead press: 3x8 @ RPE 6
  - 1‑arm DB row: 3x10/side @ RPE 6
  - Farmer carry: 4x30–40m, moderate load
  - Optional conditioning: 10–15 min easy walk/elliptical

Week 2
- Repeat Week 1 pattern. If all symptom‑free, add 2–3% load or +1 rep to top two sets per lift. Keep RPE ≤7.

Week 3
- Day A: Safety bar squat 5x4 @ RPE 6–7; DB RDL 3x8; Landmine press 3x8/side; Lat pulldown 3x8; Side plank 3x25–35s.
- Day B: Trap bar deadlift 5x3 @ RPE 6–7; Incline DB press 4x6–7; Chest‑supported row 3x10; Split squat 3x8/side; Pallof press 3x10/side (add band tension).
- Day C: Goblet squat (heavier) 4x6 @ RPE 6–7; Cable pull‑through 3x10; Seated DB press 3x8–10; 1‑arm DB row 3x10–12; Suitcase carry 4x30m/side.

Week 4 (deload/hold)
- Reduce volume 20–30% or keep loads but do 1 fewer set on main lifts. Maintain movement quality. Keep conditioning light 10–15 min.

Phase 2: Weeks 5–8 (maintain strength, emphasize unilateral control)
Week 5
- Day A
  - High‑bar box squat (consistent depth): 4x4 @ RPE 6–7
  - Barbell or DB RDL: 4x6 @ RPE 6–7
  - Half‑kneeling landmine press: 3x8/side
  - Wide‑neutral lat pulldown: 3x8
  - Side plank with top‑leg abduction (if tolerated): 3x20s/side
- Day B
  - Trap bar deadlift: 4x3–4 @ RPE 6–7
  - Incline barbell press or machine chest press: 4x5–6 @ RPE 6–7
  - Cable row (neutral): 3x8–10
  - Rear‑foot elevated split squat (short stance): 3x6–8/side
  - Pallof iso hold: 3x20–30s/side
- Day C
  - Step‑ups (knee height just below hip): 4x6/side
  - Landmine RDL: 3x8
  - Seated DB press (slight back support): 3x8
  - 1‑arm cable row (split stance): 3x10/side
  - Farmer carry: 4x40m

Week 6
- Same structure. Progress small if RPE ≤6. Option to add one back‑off set at −5–7% load for main lift. Monitor ligament laxity; keep tempo controlled (2–0–2).

Week 7
- Day A: Safety bar squat 5x3 @ RPE 6–7; DB RDL 3x8; Half‑kneeling landmine press 3x8/side; Lat pulldown 3x8–10; Side plank 3x25–35s.
- Day B: Trap bar deadlift 5x2–3 @ RPE 6–7; Incline DB press 4x6; Chest‑supported row 3x10; Split squat 3x8/side; Pallof press 3x10/side.
- Day C: Goblet squat 4x6–8; Cable pull‑through 3x10–12; Seated DB press 3x8–10; 1‑arm DB row 3x10–12; Suitcase carry 4x30–40m/side.

Week 8 (deload/hold)
- Cut one set from main patterns; maintain accessories. Add extra mobility for hips/thoracic. Keep RPE ≤6 across.

Phase 3: Weeks 9–12 (hold strength, joint comfort, birth‑supportive breathing)
Week 9
- Day A
  - Box squat (safety bar or goblet): 4x4 @ RPE 6–7
  - Hip hinge: Cable pull‑through or light RDL 3x10 @ RPE 6
  - Landmine press (standing, slight stagger): 3x8/side
  - Lat pulldown: 3x8–10
  - Side plank elevated or Copenhagen short‑lever (if comfy): 3x15–20s/side
- Day B
  - Trap bar deadlift (technique focus): 4x2–3 @ RPE 6
  - Incline press (DB): 4x5–6 @ RPE 6–7
  - Chest‑supported row: 3x10–12
  - Step‑downs (low box): 3x8/side
  - Pallof press with overhead reach: 3x8/side
- Day C
  - Split squat (rear foot on floor): 4x6/side
  - Landmine RDL: 3x8–10
  - Seated DB press: 3x8
  - 1‑arm cable row: 3x10/side
  - Farmer or suitcase carry: 4x30–40m

Week 10
- Maintain loads or micro‑progress if RPE ≤6 and energy good. Emphasize long exhales (4–6s) through concentric, gentle pelvic floor lift.

Week 11
- Day A: Goblet box squat 4x6 @ RPE 6; DB RDL 3x8; Landmine press 3x8/side; Pulldown 3x10; Side plank 3x20–30s.
- Day B: Trap bar deadlift 3x3 @ RPE 6; Incline press 3x6; Cable row 3x10; Step‑ups 3x8/side; Pallof press 3x10/side.
- Day C: Split squat 3x6/side; Cable pull‑through 3x10–12; Seated DB press 3x8; 1‑arm DB row 3x10–12; Suitcase carry 3x30m/side.
- Note: If any pubic symphysis discomfort arises, narrow squat stance, reduce single‑leg ROM, prefer box squats and step‑ups over lunges.

Week 12 (taper/comfort week)
- Keep the same exercise menu; reduce volume by 25–40% (fewer sets, keep loads comfortable). Focus on easy wins, mobility, and breathing.

Core and breathing mini‑circuit options (2–3 rounds at end, most sessions)
- A: Pallof press 8–10/side, Side plank 20–30s/side, Bird dog 6–8/side (slow)
- B: Half‑kneeling anti‑rotation press 8–10/side, Suitcase carry 30–40m/side, Wall slides 10
- C: Seated or elevated dead bug pattern 6–8/side (no doming), Banded pull‑apart 12–15, Diaphragmatic breaths 5 slow cycles

Conditioning (2–3x/week, can be after lifting or separate)
- 10–20 minutes at conversational pace: treadmill walk (slight incline), bike (upright), elliptical. RPE 4–5/10. Stop if overheating or dizzy.

Accessory/posture work sprinkled 2–3x/week
- Band pull‑aparts or wall slides 2x12–15
- Gentle thoracic extension over foam roller 1–2 minutes
- Hip airplanes (supported) 2x5/side, only if stable/pain‑free

Recovery and lifestyle
- Daily walks 10–20 minutes if comfortable.
- After sessions: 3–5 minutes easy breathing and gentle mobility.
- Pelvic floor: Practice “relax on inhale, lift gently on exhale” during reps and 2–3 minutes daily. Late in program, also practice full relaxation on long exhales to prepare for labor.
- Footwear: Supportive shoes; consider wider stance and toe‑out as needed.
- Belts/straps: Light belt use only if it helps position awareness; avoid maximal bracing. Lifting straps fine if grip fatigues.

Nutrition (general pregnancy‑safe training guidance; defer to clinician for individualized targets)
- Aim for sufficient energy intake to match pregnancy needs and training. Typical second trimester adds ~340 kcal/day; third trimester ~450 kcal/day. Let hunger/weight‑gain targets from OB/midwife guide adjustments.
- Protein: ~1.2–1.5 g/kg/day spread over 3–5 meals; include leucine‑rich sources. Pair with carbs pre/post‑training for energy and recovery.
- Hydration: 2.5–3+ L/day; include electrolytes if sweating more.
- Pre‑session snack: 30–60 g carbs + 10–20 g protein 60–90 min pre. Post: 20–30 g protein + 40–60 g carbs within 1–2 hours if appetite allows.
- Supplements: Continue prenatal per provider. Avoid new ergogenics. Creatine monohydrate is sometimes used in pregnancy but only continue/start with OB approval.

Monitoring and communication
- Use a simple readiness check each session: sleep, energy, soreness, pelvic symptoms. If 2 or more are “poor,” hold loads, reduce sets, or swap to movement prep + accessories.
- Keep a symptom log (doming, pelvic pressure, incontinence, pain) and adjust exercises immediately if present.
- Plan to reassess stance widths, ROM, and exercise comfort weekly as bump grows; swap to machines or dumbbells when bar path feels crowded.

This plan keeps her strong, emphasizes technique, and adapts progressively to pregnancy changes while staying within moderate intensity and safety parameters. Adjust in real time based on her daily readiness and OB/midwife guidance.
